1) SOC 2 evidence cadence — can you confirm the cadence you intend to provide (monthly vs quarterly exports) and an example set of artefacts we can expect (control owner mapping, last report, exception logs, retentions)?

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear asks. Quick summary below and next steps.

1) SOC 2 evidence cadence: we publish an annual SOC 2 Type II report. For operational evidence we can provide a quarterly evidence bundle (CSV index + PDFs) with a one-week lead for collection. The bundle typically includes: control mapping, last three months of audit logs (redacted where needed), backup verification checks, and a list of remediation tickets for exceptions. If Atlas needs monthly exports, we can support that for an enterprise addendum — I'll loop Laura for the delivery SLA.

2) Pen test window: Redwood proposes two candidate windows in June — Jun 10–16 or Jun 24–30 for a staging-only penetration test. Tests should be zero-impact to production; we'll provide a staging endpoint, static IP allowlist, and temporary service accounts scoped to the test. Please see attached: proposed-pen-test-windows.xlsx (contains IP ranges, contact matrix, and proposed blackout hours).

Next steps:
- Laura, can you confirm evidence bundle format and whether quarterly is acceptable by default?
- Karthik, legal has a few redlines to security exhibit section 4 (inspection rights and notice). Can you weigh in on acceptable notice windows for pen tests (48–72 hours vs 7 days) and any obligatory notifications?
- Emily / Sam, if one of the June windows works, we can lock and build the staging access ticket.

Best,
Priya

Thanks Priya and Emily. Internal notes and legal posture below.

SOC 2 evidence cadence: quarterly evidence bundle is our standard offer for hosted customers; the bundle is assembled by our compliance team and includes the items Priya listed. We can add a monthly delta-report for customers who need closer monitoring (this would be a paid add-on; I'll note pricing). For the order form, we'll add a line item: "Evidence cadence: quarterly, optional monthly delta-report" and reference the Exhibit A evidence index.

Pen test / inspection rights (legal): 
- Redwood proposes a 72-hour notice for scheduled penetration testing if the test is non-production and uses only staging endpoints.
- For customer-requested production tests, we require a 7-day notice and an SOW specifying scope, insurance, and rollback plans.
- We will not accept unscheduled inspections or requests that demand system-level access beyond the provided staging accounts.

Marissa is copying in operational runbook items and will own the runbook that lists required artifacts from Atlas (allowed IPs, minimal sample dataset, test accounts).

Karthik — legal redlines: we need to soften the blanket "audit at any time" language in the exhibit. Proposed insertion:
"Inspection rights: Customer may request scheduled inspections reasonable for compliance; Redwood will provide reasonable access to staging and documentation. All production access requests require 7 days' notice and mutually agreed scope."

Laura Bennett
Head of Compliance Operations — Redwood Inference

Priya / Laura — appreciate the quick turnaround. A few clarifying points from Atlas:  

- Quarterly evidence bundle acceptable by default. Atlas requests two sample artifacts up front so our SOC team can validate format before we sign (sample control mapping + sample audit log with redactions). Can you provide samples by EOD Tuesday?
- Pen test: Jun 10–16 is preferable. The procurement team requires 72-hour notice before the start of the test and confirmation that the staging environment mirrors production authentication flows (SSO).
- Regarding inspection rights: legal at Atlas will not accept a clause that prevents production testing under any circumstances. They need a path for limited production testing with a formal SOW and indemnities. Will Redwood accept a carve-out for emergency production inspections tied to incident response?

We are close — if we align on samples and the test window, procurement will finish the order form sign-off.

Thanks,
Emily

Emily — quick follow-up from legal with a proposed clause we can add to the exhibit to address the "limited production testing" ask. We want to avoid open-ended rights but are willing to accept a controlled path: 

"Emergency inspection carve-out: In the event of a material security incident that reasonably indicates customer data exposure, Redwood will cooperate with Customer and may provide controlled, read-only access to affected subsystems under a signed SOW that limits scope, duration, and access methods. Any such access will require mutual approval of the SOW and reasonable safeguards including data minimization and escrowed logs. Production testing that could materially affect availability or integrity will require a separate SOW and seven (7) days' prior written notice unless the parties agree otherwise in writing.

If that language is acceptable, we will:
- Insert it into Exhibit B (inspection & pen test language) as a new paragraph;
- Confirm the June 10–16 staging window and create the staging-ticket;
- Deliver two sample artifacts (control mapping & redacted audit log) by EOD Tuesday as requested.

If Atlas legal needs different wording, please propose edits in-track and we will try to resolve quickly.
